gaudiya_vaishnava.source: Hari-bhakti-vilāsa · Sanātana Gosvāmī (16th c.) · Arcana-dīpikā · Gaudiya Vedanta Publications
gaudiya_vaishnava.relationship: eternal devotee of Kṛṣṇa · not a herb but a person
gaudiya_vaishnava.note: She is addressed as a person. She participates in worship. This is observed practice from living Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition.
gaudiya_vaishnava.primary_text_passage: After bathing and performing āhnika (the chanting of the dīkṣā-mantras), bathe tulasī [by pouring water on her soil], while chanting her bathing mantra. Then offer her praṇāma while chanting her praṇāma-mantra. Then, while chanting the mantra for picking tulasī (cayana-mantra), pick the leaf that is joined with the stem, or else pick soft mañjarīs (flower buds) that are joined with the leaves and stem.
gaudiya_vaishnava.primary_text_rule: For pure Vaiṣṇavas though, picking tulasī is only prohibited on the day of Dvādaśī.
gaudiya_vaishnava.primary_text_restriction: One should not pick flowers or tulasī once the sun has started to set.

synthesis.content: Three irreducible relationships coexist: medicinal (Charaka / Āyurveda), devotional (Hari-bhakti-vilāsa / Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava), and ecological (PFAF / permaculture). None generates the others. All are OBSERVED in their own domain. The ethnobotanical description from PFAF overlaps with but is not identical to the Āyurvedic account — they share the plant but not the framework.
